Madhav Mandal And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. on 2 January,
2024
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad 
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:136
Court No. - 84
Case :- Criminal Appeal No. - 4361 of 2022 
Appellant :- Madhav Mandal And 2 Others 
Respondent :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Appellant :- Anand Kumar Singh,Roshni Murad,Suraj Kumar Singh 
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Nalin Kumar Srivastava,J.
Order on Criminal Misc. Bail Application 
1.  This Criminal appeal under Section 374 (2) of the Criminal Procedure Code has been preferred by the appellants Madhav Mandal, Taposh Sikandar & Sapan Vishwas against the conviction and sentence recorded vide judgment and order dated 30.05.2022 passed by the Additional District and Sessions Judge, Court No.5, Varanasi in Sessions Trial No.508 of 2021, arising out of case crime no.53 of 2021, under Sections 188, 273 I.P.C. and Section 31(1)/63 Food Safety Standard Act, P.S.
Lanka, District Varanasi wherein the maximum punishment was imposed upon the appellants under Section 273 I.P.C. for imprisonment of ten years. 
2. Heard learned Counsel for the appellants-applicants as well as the learned AGA for the State.
3. By means of the bail application, the appellants-applicants seeks suspension of sentence and Madhav Mandal And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46118806/
1 grant of bail. 
4. It has been submitted by learned counsel for the appellants-applicants that the appellants are innocent and have falsely been implicated. It has been further submitted that the conviction and sentence imposed by the learned trial Judge is against the weight of evidence on record. The trial court has misread the evidence on record and convicted the appellants. The prosecution has not been able to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. It has been further submitted that the appellants were on bail during trial and have not misused the liberty of bail. Since there is no likelihood of early hearing of the appeal in near future, the appellants may be released on bail pending appeal. Besides the above submissions, learned counsel for the appellants has also tried to touch upon at length the circumstances which led to the false implication of accused - appellants. 
5. Learned counsel for the appellants has further submitted that the impugned judgment and order has been passed without appreciating the material evidence on record. It is further submitted that the Nayab Tehsildar, Bharat Paswan, who was leading the team at the time of abolishing Thai Mangur has not been examined during trial who was the material witness. It is next submitted that perfect examination has not been performed during the investigation of this case in respect of thai mangur which is to be resulted hazardous for human health and ecosystem. It is also submitted that the relevant provision of Food Safety Standard Act has also not been promulgated by the trial court in proper manner. It is next submitted that the appellants have no criminal antecedents to their credit nor anything to this effect has been brought into light by the learned A.G.A. in the counter affidavit. It is next submitted that the appellants are languishing in jail since 30.05.2022.
6. On the other hand, learned AGA vehemently opposed the bail application but however he could not dispute the factual aspect of the matter as submitted by the learned counsel for the appellants. 
7. I have considered the rival submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the entire record including the impugned judgment. 
8. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, sentence awarded to the appellants, the evidence available on record and the findings recorded by the trial court thereon, appellants were on bail during trial but no instance of misuse of the bail has been brought to the notice of the Court and the fact that the appeal may take some time for its final disposal, without further commenting on the merits of the case, I am inclined to release the appellants on bail.
9. Let the above named accused-appellants be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of Court concerned. 
10. On acceptance of bail bond and personal bonds, the lower court shall transmit photostat copies thereof to this Court for being kept on record. 
11. However, half of the fine amount, as imposed by the trial Court, is stayed but accused-appellants shall deposit the remaining half fine within a period of two months from the date of their release in terms of the order of learned trial Court.

2 12. List this appeal in its due course.
